chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who prayed and remembered that he had added an extra prostration. He said: 'He does not repeat the prayer if the extra prostration was in a single rak'ah, but he must repeat it if it was from a rak'ah (i.e., added to a different rak'ah or caused confusion between them).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person adds an extra prostration during prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *sahw* (forgetfulness) in prayer, distinguishing between an error that remains within the structural integrity of a rak'ah versus one that alters the total count of rak'ahs. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the leniency applied to minor structural deviations, ensuring that the prayer is not invalidated unless the fundamental sequence is compromised. This distinction underscores the practical ease (*taysir*) intended by the Imams for the worshippers.
